chunks: Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Bukayr, from Hamzah ibn Muhammad, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: "And guided him to the two conspicuous ways." He (AS) said: "The way of good and the way of evil."

key_terms.النَّجْدَيْنِ: The two conspicuous ways (of good and evil)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'the two conspicuous ways' (al-najdayn) refer to in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this concise exegesis from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that 'the two ways' (al-najdayn) in Surah Al-Balad refer specifically to the distinct paths of good and evil, emphasizing the innate human capacity for moral discernment. This interpretation underscores the Shia theological principle of *fitrah* and the balance between divine guidance and human free will, illustrating how God facilitates the recognition of these dual paths for every individual.
